structure_explanation.en: Here we have the passive voice combined with the 〜ている form, which indicates a continuous or habitual state. The topic is この歌 (marked by は), the agent is みんな ('everyone', with に), and 歌う ('to sing') becomes 歌われている ('is/has been being sung'). The focus is the passive 〜れる; the ている shows the action happens continuously/recurrently.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Aqui temos a voz passiva combinada com a forma 〜ている, que indica um estado contínuo ou habitual. O tópico é この歌 (marcado por は), o agente é みんな ('todos', com に), e 歌う ('cantar') vira 歌われている ('é/vem sendo cantada'). O foco é a passiva 〜れる; o ている mostra que a ação acontece de forma contínua/recorrente.

ops.issue: In the fixed casual farewell じゃあ、また明日, 明日 is read あした. あす is formal/literary and clashes with the casual register the expl itself describes; natives do not say 'mata asu' as a goodbye. Romaji 'mataasu' inherits the error.
Token reading for 明日 in the casual set phrase また明日 should be あした, not the formal/literary あす.

before.jp: じゃあ、また明日
before.kana: じゃあ、またあす

structure_explanation.en: It is a casual goodbye made of fixed words, with no verb. じゃあ ('well, then') signals closing, and また明日 ('see you tomorrow', literally 'again tomorrow') is the standard parting phrase. The target is the connector じゃあ, typical of informal speech.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: É uma despedida casual feita de palavras fixas, sem verbo. じゃあ ('bom, então') sinaliza encerramento, e また明日 ('até amanhã', literalmente 'de novo amanhã') é a expressão padrão de despedida. O alvo é o conector じゃあ, típico da fala informal.

ops.issue: 三時頃 is read さんじごろ (頃 takes rendaku ごろ after a specific time). The item's own expl_en/expl_pt explicitly state this rule ('read ごろ when it comes after an exact time'), yet the kana says ころ. Romaji 'sanjikoroni...' inherits the same error.
Token reading for 頃 after 三時 must be ごろ (rendaku), not ころ; contradicts the record's own explanation of the 頃/ごろ rule.

before.jp: 三時頃に駅で会いましょう
before.kana: さんじころにえきであいましょう

structure_explanation.en: The focus is the target pattern 頃, read ごろ when it comes after an exact time: 三時頃 = 'around three o'clock,' indicating an approximate time. Then come two places/times marked by particles: に fixes the point in time and で marks the place of the action. The verb ends in 会いましょう (the polite volitional form of 会う), which invites: 'let's meet.'
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O foco é o padrão-alvo 頃, lido ごろ quando vem depois de um horário exato: 三時頃 = 'por volta das três horas', indicando hora aproximada. Depois vêm dois lugares/momentos marcados por partículas: に fixa o ponto no tempo e で marca o local da ação. O verbo termina em 会いましょう (forma volitiva polida de 会う), que convida: 'vamos nos encontrar'.

ops.issue: その ('that', near the listener) translated as 'these', reversing deixis; contradicts the token gloss 'that, that one' and the pt 'essa roupa'. Deixis is a core teaching point.
Literal field is inaccurate: adds 'too' (no 〜すぎる in the JP) and drops the final よ that lit_pt renders ('viu'); also loses the topic marking that lit_pt mirrors.

before.jp: 雨の日にその格好は寒いよ
before.kana: あめのひにそのかっこうわさむいよ

structure_explanation.en: 「雨の日に」 forms a time expression: 雨 ('rain') + の linking to the noun 日 ('day'), and に marking the moment ('on a rainy day'). Then, 「その格好は」 brings the topic (その = 'that' + 格好 = 'clothes/attire'), marked by は. The predicate is the い-adjective 寒い ('cold'), and the final particle よ adds a friendly warning tone ('you know', 'look').
structure_explanation.pt-BR: 「雨の日に」 forma uma expressão de tempo: 雨 ('chuva') + の ligando ao substantivo 日 ('dia'), e に marcando o momento ('em dia de chuva'). Depois, 「その格好は」 traz o tópico (その = 'essa/aquela' + 格好 = 'roupa/traje'), marcado por は. O predicado é o い-adjetivo 寒い ('frio'), e a partícula final よ acrescenta um tom de aviso amigável ('viu', 'olha').

translation_literal.en: On a rainy day, those clothes are too cold.
